questions.q: Design a multi-tenant SaaS application with Laravel.
questions.a:
Two approaches:

Single database (row-level):
â€¢ All tenants share one database. Each table has tenant_id column.
â€¢ Global scope: TenantScope auto-filters where('tenant_id', currentTenant()) on all queries.
â€¢ Pros: simple infrastructure, easy migrations. Cons: data isolation risk, harder to scale.

Multi-database (database-per-tenant):
â€¢ Each tenant gets their own database. Central tenants table maps domains to databases.
â€¢ Middleware resolves tenant, sets config('database.connections.tenant.database') dynamically.
â€¢ Pros: strong isolation, can backup/restore per tenant. Cons: complex migrations, higher resource usage.

Key considerations:
â€¢ Domain routing: Route::domain('{tenant}.app.com') or header-based
â€¢ Cache isolation: prefix cache keys with tenant ID
â€¢ Queue isolation: separate queue per tenant or use tenant_id in job metadata
â€¢ File storage: directories per tenant on S3 (tenants/{id}/)
â€¢ Testing: ensure tenant-scoped tests don't leak data between test suites

questions.q: Design a shopping cart that persists across guest sessions and login merge.
questions.a:
Approach:

Database:
Cart model: user_id (nullable), session_id, product_id, quantity, created_at.

CartService:
â€¢ addItem(productId, quantity) â€” upsert by product
â€¢ removeItem(productId)
â€¢ getTotal() â€” sum of (price Ã— quantity)
â€¢ clear()

Guest flow: cart stored with session_id only. Data loaded on every page via ViewComposer or middleware.

Login merge: on Login event, call CartService::mergeCarts(sessionCart, userCart):
â€¢ For each guest item: if user has same product, sum quantities (capped at stock). Else, attach to user.

questions.q: Design a multi-step form with data persistence across sessions.
questions.a:
Approach:
â€¢ UserRegistration model with JSON data column, current_step (int), completed (bool)
â€¢ Each step validates its own subset of fields before advancing
â€¢ Temporary data stored in session, persisted to DB only on final step
â€¢ On step advance: merge validated data into JSON column, increment step
â€¢ On back: restore from DB/session without re-validating

Implementation:
public function store(Request $request, $step) {
$validated = $request->validate(StepValidation::rules()[$step]);
$registration = UserRegistration::findOrFail(session('registration_id'));
$data = array_merge($registration->data ?? [], $validated);
$registration->update(['data' => $data, 'current_step' => $step]);
if ($step === StepValidation::LAST_STEP) {
$registration->update(['completed' => true]);
event(new RegistrationCompleted($registration));
}
}

Edge cases:
â€¢ Browser closed mid-form â†’ recover from DB using session token
â€¢ Expired sessions â†’ clean up with scheduled job (weekly)
â€¢ Back button â†’ restore prior step data without re-validation
â€¢ Concurrent submissions â†’ use row lock to prevent overwrite
â€¢ File uploads in intermediate steps â†’ store temp files, clean on abandon

questions.q: Design a role-based access control (RBAC) system.
questions.a:
Approach:
â€¢ Role (belongsToMany users), Permission (belongsToMany roles)
â€¢ Pivot tables: role_user, permission_role
â€¢ User model has permissions through roles

Authorization layer:
Gate::define('edit-post', fn($user, $post) =>
$user->hasPermission('edit-posts') || $user->id === $post->user_id
);

Cache strategy:
public function hasPermission($perm): bool {
return Cache::remember('user.' . $this->id . '.permissions', 3600, function () use ($perm) {
return $this->roles->pluck('permissions')->flatten()->pluck('slug')->contains($perm);
});
}

Middleware:
Route::middleware('role:admin,editor')

Edge cases:
â€¢ Circular permissions â†’ keep role-permission hierarchy flat
â€¢ Super admin â†’ explicit bypass check at top of hasPermission()
â€¢ Cache invalidation â†’ clear cache on role/permission assignment
â€¢ Soft-deleted roles â†’ exclude from query, notify admins

questions.q: Build a RESTful API with pagination, filtering, and sorting.
questions.a:
Approach:
â€¢ Use query builder with conditional when() for dynamic filters
â€¢ Whitelist allowed sort columns to prevent SQL injection
â€¢ API Resource collection for consistent response transformation
â€¢ Form Request validation for query string parameters

Controller example:
public function index(ProductIndexRequest $request) {
return Product::query()
->when($request->category_id, fn($q, $v) => $q->where('category_id', $v))
->when($request->min_price, fn($q, $v) => $q->where('price', '>=', $v))
->when($request->in_stock, fn($q, $v) => $q->where('stock', '>', 0))
->when($request->sort, fn($q, $v) => in_array($v, ['name','price','created_at']) ? $q->orderBy($v, $request->direction ?? 'asc') : $q)
->paginate($request->per_page ?? 15);
}

Edge cases:
â€¢ Invalid sort field â†’ return 422 with clear error
â€¢ SQL injection via sort â†’ whitelist prevents raw column names
â€¢ Very large datasets â†’ enforce max per_page, use cursor pagination
â€¢ Empty results â†’ return empty data array, not 404
â€¢ N+1 on relationships â†’ use with() for common includes

questions.q: Design a file upload system with image optimization and CDN delivery.
questions.a:
Approach:
â€¢ Intervention Image for resize + optimize
â€¢ S3 storage with CloudFront CDN
â€¢ Queue resize/optimization jobs for async processing
â€¢ Polymorphic Media table for attachment to any model

Validation:
'file' => 'required|image|mimes:jpg,png,webp|max:2048'

Upload + queue:
$path = $request->file('file')->store('uploads/' . date('Y/m'), 's3');
$media = Media::create([
'path' => $path, 'disk' => 's3',
'mime_type' => $request->file('file')->getMimeType(),
'size' => $request->file('file')->getSize(),
]);
OptimizeImage::dispatch($media);

Edge cases:
â€¢ Malicious file upload â†’ validate MIME + scan with ClamAV
â€¢ Disk quota â†’ check user storage usage before accepting
â€¢ CDN cache purge â†’ CloudFront invalidation after update/delete
â€¢ Concurrent resize â†’ queue deduplication (uniqueBy media_id)
â€¢ EXIF data stripping â†’ remove before storing for privacy
